## About

The viewer styled from a stylesheet. `css-class` adds a class to the
viewer, and `n-css-class.css` uses it to set the viewer's colors (plum,
with pink links), draw a line along the top of the caption band, and make
the caption larger and italic.

```yaml
format:
  html:
    css: n-css-class.css
panzoom:
  css-class: plum-viewer
```

Only pages with that class get the rules, so the other pages of the site
keep the default viewer. A single image or code cell can add a class of
its own, as cases 2 and 4 show; it applies while that image is open.

The page uses this stylesheet:

```css
.plum-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #2d1236;
  --panzoom-fg: #f3e8f7;
  --panzoom-link: #ffb3d9;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top: 4px solid #d58cf0;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  font-style: italic;
}
.sea-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #0f3640;
  --panzoom-fg: #e0f4f7;
  --panzoom-link: #7fe0d0;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top-color: #4fc3c9;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-style: normal;
}
```

Rules on the viewer's parts start with the viewer's class, as above, so
they win over the defaults. The parts are `.panzoom-footer` (the caption
band), `.panzoom-caption`, `.panzoom-description`, `.panzoom-hint`,
`.panzoom-close`, `.panzoom-prev`, `.panzoom-next`, and `.panzoom-counter`.

For a whole site, put `css-class` (or any option) under `format: html:` in
`_quarto.yml`. A top-level `panzoom:` there is replaced, not merged, by a
page's own `panzoom:` options.

## 1. Marked image {#c1 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

A marked image with a link in its caption. It opens in panzoom with the plum
viewer from the stylesheet, a pink link, a line along the top of the caption
band, and a larger, italic caption.

```{.markdown .show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`. It opens with the plum viewer from the stylesheet, a line along the top of the caption band, a larger, italic caption, and this pink [link](https://quarto.org).](../../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom}
```

## 2. Class for one image {#c2 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

The page's class stays on the viewer, so rules for `.sea-viewer` come after
the `.plum-viewer` ones to win over them.

```{.markdown .show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`, with a class of its own, `css-class="sea-viewer"`. It opens with the dark teal `.sea-viewer` rules and an upright caption, and this [link](https://quarto.org) is teal.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom css-class="sea-viewer"}
```

## 3. Code cell {#c3 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A code cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens with the plum viewer, as case 1 does."

plot(pressure, type = "b", pch = 19)
```

## 4. Class for one cell {#c4 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   css-class: sea-viewer
#| fig-cap: "A code cell with `css-class: sea-viewer` under `#| panzoom:`. It opens with the same teal viewer as case 2."

plot(cars, pch = 19)
```
